title: Build your own local asset generators, do not pay for tools or waste tokens
author: W3103_
selftext:
(posting this after some requests in comment section, and some people saying I've made it up)   
  
  
Last night Claude built a simple, intuitive and working LOCAL image to 3d asset generator with a simple prompt. I am not a pro dev, I am a normal working guy who is an idiot, with a fun vibecoding hobby

If you're trying to get custom assets, and you have Claude code. It is easier than you think! Ask it to make one! 

Here's the very general prompt I worded vomited into my microphone last night: 

So is it possible to make a program that we can use to make our models a bit better? So I'm thinking if we make our own machine that can convert images to 3d models. basically I've found a few tools that can do it, like tripo. So it seems like it's something that we can make. 

I want it so I can upload a picture of for example, a  fish into the machine and it will make the perfect asset of that fish for the game, and then it's just literally a matter of saying to you okay that's done take that file, And then you can ship it to the game, and configure its skeleton and movement. And it communicates with the game development. And basically says, to the main Claude coding session, here's the fish or Whatever it is. 

 Because I think if we build the models on this app instead, it will make them look better and it's tokens for you, if the app is actually doing it itself every time.  Is that possible to build?

replies.author: W3103_
replies.body:
hunyuan’s licence doesn’t cover the uk so that was out, and trellis is a pain on an amd card so i made an app that would work for me. it cuts the photo out, turns the model into lower poly style, paints it from the photo, exports it ready for my game, builds the movement and skeleton, and drops it straight in.   
  
drag a photo in and 3 mins later it’s a fish in my game. if you just want a raw model then yeah, comfyui does the job

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body:
You need to separate and focus. I see a lot of people try to generate entire body models when you should approach it more like you would 3D printing. Face closeup for details, lower "voxel size", etc. TRELLIS 2 is not magic, so is Tripo and Meshy, their UV packing and unwrapping are awful and their topology is awful by any professional standard, so it depends on what good results mean here.

If you know your way around 3D it's a very good starting base to retopo and texture for basically free if you got the GPUs.

replies.author: UnimagineDragons
replies.body:
I did something slightly different. I have a laptop with a mobile 3060 I use as my generator. I have Claude on it and gave  a similar prompt and it pointed me to local model generation. We settled on Hyunyuan3D. With the 6gb vram I have it wanted to stick to just outlines/shaped but adding color/texters works too. 

Claude makes sprites (on Gemini) in T pose (for player characters with fighting animation) or other pose,  adds skeleton in Adobe Mixamo, then repaints the "shape" with the sprites. It gives a cool 3d yet illustrated look.

The model (if you missed above) I use is Hyunyuan3D

comments.author: ZHName
comments.body:
I tried something like this for a prompt: 

1. Use FluxKlein2 or Krea to generate character sheet, use removebg to clean up OR create a sheet of PARTS for \[xyz asset like space ship, crate, outfit\]

2. Pass the character sheet(or part) to tripo or whatever, best params for low poly to mid-poly detail

3. Evaluate quality against the character sheet / part image from FluxKlein or Krea

Depending on RAM available, you may run into OOM issues and garbled models. I'm not sure if my settings but sometimes the models are better than at other times. For basic things, I think it is doable locally 100%, even without using any API for kits.

comments.author: droid_man_
comments.body:
I've been dealing with that exact same problem for over a month now, and I've found a lot of models that let you generate 3D models locally. Unfortunately for me, I have an AMD graphics card that doesn't support CUDA, which really limits my options. I'm thinking about upgrading to an RTX 5070 Ti so I can run TRELLIS, Pi3D, and Hunyuan3D locally without any issues.

I even tried a setup using Claude with Opus 5.5 on Max, UltraCode, and pretty much everything enabled. It actually works quite well, but there's one major problem: the 3D models aren't low-poly enough for games, which causes performance issues.

So I also tried generating the models in separate parts, creating modular 3D models instead. The results are actually pretty good, especially for games where I want to give players the ability to swap out parts or add different equipment.
